items.requirement: Identify the review as a mixed-methods review protocol.
items.prompt: What is the mixed-methods review title and why does it require both quantitative and qualitative evidence?
items.helpText: The title should signal the mixed-methods nature of the synthesis.
items.exampleResponse: Mixed-methods review protocol: effectiveness and acceptability of community-based diabetes self-management interventions.

items.prompt: Why must quantitative and qualitative evidence be integrated for this question?
items.helpText: Explain what each evidence stream contributes and why integration matters.
items.exampleResponse: Effect estimates will show whether interventions work, while qualitative evidence will explain acceptability and implementation conditions.

items.requirement: State quantitative, qualitative, and integrated questions.
items.prompt: What are the quantitative question, qualitative question, and integrated mixed-methods question?
items.helpText: Avoid a mismatch between the questions and the planned integration method.
items.exampleResponse: Quantitative: What is the effect on HbA1c? Qualitative: What shapes acceptability? Integrated: Which intervention features appear effective and acceptable?

items.requirement: State the review objectives clearly and in alignment with the review type.
items.prompt: What are the primary and secondary objectives this protocol will guide?
items.helpText: Objectives should match the review type: estimate, map, explain, synthesize experiences, compare reviews, or maintain living evidence. Separate quantitative, qualitative, and integrated objectives.
items.exampleResponse: The primary objective is to synthesize the available evidence for the defined question. Secondary objectives include identifying gaps and describing implications for decision-makers.

items.requirement: Specify eligibility for quantitative, qualitative, and mixed-methods studies.
items.prompt: Which study designs and evidence components will be eligible for each evidence stream?
items.helpText: Clarify how mixed-methods primary studies will be separated or integrated.
items.exampleResponse: We will include randomized, quasi-experimental, qualitative, and mixed-methods studies with extractable quantitative or qualitative data.

items.prompt: Which databases, repositories, registers, websites, expert sources, and grey literature sources will be searched?
items.helpText: Information sources should fit the review type and include enough coverage to reduce avoidable bias. Information sources should fit the review type and include enough coverage to reduce avoidable bias.
items.exampleResponse: We will search bibliographic databases, specialist registers, organizational repositories, relevant websites, and reference lists of included sources.

items.requirement: Describe how searches will be developed, documented, and updated if needed.
items.prompt: How will the search strategy be constructed, peer reviewed, limited, documented, and updated?
items.helpText: Include core concepts, controlled vocabulary, limits, search dates, peer review, and supplementary search methods. Ensure the strategy can identify both quantitative effectiveness evidence and qualitative or implementation evidence.
items.exampleResponse: The strategy will combine topic concepts with appropriate subject headings, document all limits, and be adapted for each database.

items.prompt: How will records or sources be screened and selected, and how will disagreements or uncertainty be handled?
items.helpText: Specify screening stages, reviewer numbers, piloting or calibration, software, reasons for exclusion, and documentation. Describe how quantitative, qualitative, and mixed-methods records will be classified during screening.
items.exampleResponse: Screening criteria will be piloted. Records will be screened at title/abstract and full-text stages, with disagreements resolved by discussion or a third reviewer.

items.prompt: What quantitative and qualitative data will be extracted, and will any data transformation be performed?
items.helpText: JBI mixed-methods guidance often distinguishes convergent integrated and convergent segregated approaches.
items.exampleResponse: Effect estimates and qualitative findings will be extracted separately; qualitative findings may be configured with quantitative result categories during integration.

items.prompt: Which tools will appraise quantitative, qualitative, and mixed-methods evidence?
items.helpText: Use design-appropriate tools and state how appraisal affects synthesis.
items.exampleResponse: Randomized studies will use RoB 2, qualitative studies CASP, and mixed-methods studies MMAT.

items.prompt: Will synthesis be convergent integrated, convergent segregated, or sequential, and how will findings be integrated?
items.helpText: Name the integration method, not just the individual synthesis methods.
items.exampleResponse: We will use a convergent segregated design, synthesize quantitative and qualitative evidence separately, then integrate through a joint display.

items.requirement: Plan certainty or confidence assessment for integrated findings.
items.prompt: How will certainty, confidence, or credibility be judged across the integrated evidence?
items.helpText: Consider GRADE for quantitative findings and CERQual for qualitative findings.
items.exampleResponse: GRADE and CERQual assessments will be presented alongside integrated findings in a joint display.

items.requirement: Describe equity, context, subgroup, and applicability considerations.
items.prompt: Which equity, context, setting, population, implementation, or applicability factors must be captured in the protocol?
items.helpText: Consider geography, socioeconomic status, gender, age, disability, health system context, and implementation setting. Consider geography, socioeconomic status, gender, age, disability, health system context, and implementation setting.
items.exampleResponse: We will extract and report context and equity-relevant characteristics, including setting, population subgroup, implementation environment, and applicability considerations.

items.requirement: Describe stakeholder engagement in question refinement, interpretation, or dissemination.
items.prompt: Which stakeholders will be involved, at what stages, and how will their input influence the review?
items.helpText: Stakeholders may help refine questions, identify sources, interpret findings, or shape outputs. State whether stakeholders will help interpret integrated findings or joint displays.
items.exampleResponse: Stakeholders will be consulted during question refinement and interpretation of preliminary findings to improve relevance and usability.

items.requirement: Describe planned outputs and dissemination routes.
items.prompt: What outputs will be produced, who are the audiences, and how will findings be shared?
items.helpText: Consider manuscripts, briefs, map products, stakeholder reports, datasets, presentations, guideline inputs, and update notices. Plan outputs that communicate both effect estimates and explanatory findings.
items.exampleResponse: Findings will be shared through a manuscript, technical report, decision brief, presentation, and accessible summary for stakeholders.

items.requirement: Identify appendices required for transparency and reproducibility.
items.prompt: Which appendices will be included to document methods and decisions?
items.helpText: Appendices may include search strategies, screening forms, extraction forms, appraisal tools, coding frameworks, stakeholder materials, and amendment logs. Include joint display templates, integration rules, and separate extraction forms.
items.exampleResponse: Appendices will include database search strategies, screening forms, extraction templates, appraisal tools, coding framework, and protocol amendments.
